h1: The 6 Best Task Stools of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 6 task stools with backrests for counters, benches and standing desks, scored on height range, footrest and gas lift.
summary: The Lorell Millenia task stool is the best pick: a stated 22 to 32 inch height range, a contoured backrest and a vinyl seat that wipes clean. SUPERJARE adds a 300 lb rating with a removable backrest and footrest, and the SGS-certified gas lift model rounds out the top three. The KKTONER PU leather stool is the budget rolling option for light use.
intro: The task stool looks like a small decision and turns into a daily one. A stool that is too low forces you to hunch at a counter, and one that is too tall leaves your feet dangling. The height range printed on the listing, and whether a footrest ring comes with it, matter more than the cushion, because they decide where your legs and back end up.

We reviewed six stools with backrests, ranging from a commercial vinyl stool to light-duty rolling models, using their listing text. Several give little hard data: only the Lorell states its height range in inches. Ranking weighs the published height range, weight rating, footrest, gas lift certification and cleaning, and we say where a listing is silent.

products.name: Lorell Millenia Series Adjustable Task Stool with Back
products.verdict: A stated 22 to 32 inch height range, a contoured back and a vinyl seat that cleans easily.
products.description:
The Lorell Millenia stool adjusts from 22 to 32 inches, fits multiple work surfaces, has a contoured backrest and a durable vinyl seat that resists wear and cleans easily.

It is the only stool here that prints its height range in inches, which lets you check it against a bench before buying. Vinyl suits labs, workshops and kitchens where spills happen. It costs the most, a tier above everything else.

Buy it for a bench or counter you use daily. The caveat is that the listing states no weight rating or footrest.

products.name: SUPERJARE Drafting Chair with Backrest
products.verdict: A 300 lb stated capacity, 360 degree swivel and a removable backrest and footrest.
products.description:
The SUPERJARE swivels 360 degrees, has adjustable height for counters, a removable backrest and footrest, and a 300 lb stated capacity on a reinforced chrome base.

A stated capacity is more than most stools here give. Removable parts let you use it as a stool for quick jobs and with a back for long sessions. It ranks below the Lorell because no height range in inches is given.

Choose it for a home workshop. The caveat is that removable parts can loosen over time.
products.skipIf: You need a published height range.

products.name: Drafting Chair with Back Support
products.verdict: An SGS-certified gas lift, a detachable backrest and footrest ring on a heavy-duty frame.
products.description:
This chair has an SGS-certified gas lift for smooth height changes, a detachable backrest and footrest ring, and a stable heavy-duty frame.

The gas lift is the part that fails first on a stool, so a certification claim is useful, though SGS testing details are the seller's own. It ranks third because no capacity or height range is stated.

Buy it for a desk or counter where the gas lift gets daily use. The caveat is the missing numbers.
products.idealFor: Daily height changes at a counter or desk.

products.name: CoVibrant Lockable Stool with Back and Foot Rest Ergonomic Rolling Hydraulic
products.verdict: A lockable rolling stool with a well-padded contoured back and a large thick seat.
products.description:
The CoVibrant is a lockable rolling stool with a hydraulic lift, a footrest, a well-padded contoured backrest and a large, thick seat. The listing also mentions safe and smooth movement.

Lockable casters are the safety feature here: a rolling stool that shifts as you sit down causes falls. The big seat is comfortable for long sessions. It ranks fourth because no capacity or height range is stated.

Choose it for a salon, studio or office. The caveat is that rolling stools demand a smooth floor.
products.skipIf: Your floor is carpeted or uneven.

products.name: Brick Attic Drafting Chair with Backrest, Adjustable Foot Rest Rolling Stool
products.verdict: An adjustable height and footrest ring with a detachable ergonomic backrest.
products.description:
The Brick Attic offers adjustable height and footrest ring height, an ergonomic detachable backrest and a rolling base.

An adjustable footrest ring helps shorter users keep their legs supported at a high bench, which a fixed ring cannot do. It ranks fifth because its listing is general and gives no capacity or lift certification.

Buy it for varied users sharing a stool at a bench, a hobby table or a salon station. The spec list is thin, so ask for the weight rating and seat height range before ordering, and check the backrest locks firmly after assembly because detachable parts loosen.
products.idealFor: Shared stools used by people of different heights.

products.name: KKTONER PU Leather Round Rolling Stool with Back Rest Height Adjustable Swivel
products.verdict: A PU leather round stool with a backrest, 360 swivel and five rolling casters.
products.description:
The KKTONER is a PU leather round rolling stool with a backrest, height adjustment, 360 degree swivel and five rolling casters.

Five casters spread the load better than four on a small base, and PU leather wipes clean. It ranks last because the listing gives no capacity or range, and it is the lowest tier.

Choose it for light home use, such as a craft desk or a kitchen counter, where its low price makes sense. PU leather can crack with age and no rating is given, so keep it away from heavy daily use and wipe it with a damp cloth rather than harsh cleaners.
products.skipIf: You need a rated, heavy-use stool.

whatMatters.detail: A task stool must reach your counter or bench with your knees near a right angle. The Lorell prints 22 to 32 inches, which is a useful range. If a listing says only adjustable height, ask for inches, because a stool that tops out at 26 inches fits a counter badly.

On a tall stool your feet cannot reach the floor, so a ring prevents your legs from dangling and blood pooling. An adjustable ring, as on the Brick Attic, suits users of different heights. Check for the ring and its adjustment on the listing before choosing.

The gas cylinder handles every height change and is the part that fails first. An SGS certification claim, as on the Drafting Chair with Back Support, is a sign of quality control, but it is the seller's statement. Prefer certified lifts and ask for the rating.

Rolling stools move when you sit down, which causes falls. Lockable casters, like the CoVibrant, stop that, and five casters spread load better than four. Choose locks if the floor is smooth, and fixed glides if you want a stool that stays put. Test the lock by pushing sideways before you trust it with your weight, every time you sit down.

Vinyl and PU leather wipe clean, which suits workshops and kitchens, but PU can crack and peel with age. Vinyl, as on the Lorell, is typically tougher. Choose a wipe-clean cover for messy places, and fabric only for dry offices. Check the listing for the cover name, because a seat simply called leather-look may be a thin coating over foam.

faq.q: Do these stools fit standing desks?
faq.a: Possibly. The Lorell lists a 22 to 32 inch range for multiple work surfaces. For a tall standing desk, check that the maximum seat height reaches yours, since other listings give no range.

faq.q: What is the common mistake with task stools?
faq.a: Buying without checking the height range. A stool that tops out too low leaves you hunched. Only the Lorell prints its range, so ask sellers of the others for the minimum and maximum.

faq.q: Is the Lorell worth it over the SUPERJARE?
faq.a: For daily professional use, yes. The Lorell offers a published range and a wipe-clean vinyl seat. The SUPERJARE states a 300 lb capacity and a removable footrest for a lower price.
Most arrive with the gas lift, base and seat to attach. Press the seat firmly onto the lift, then fit the casters. The Brick Attic and SUPERJARE have detachable backs, so attach them last.

faq.q: How do I maintain the lift?
faq.a: Avoid dropping into the seat, keep the cylinder free of dust and replace it if the stool sinks. A certified lift, as on the Drafting Chair with Back Support, still wears with heavy use.

faq.q: Can I use a rolling stool on carpet?
faq.a: Rolling stools struggle on thick carpet. The CoVibrant and KKTONER roll best on hard floors, where lockable or five-caster bases stay steady. On carpet, use a chair mat or choose a fixed-base stool such as the Lorell.

finalTake: The Lorell Millenia task stool is the best because it is the only one that prints its height range, has a contoured back and a wipe-clean vinyl seat. The SUPERJARE is the value pick with a stated 300 lb rating. Treat every listing without a printed range or capacity as a question to ask the seller.
